TPG Growth’s Smith + Howard Acquires Hagler & Brocato and Byrne|Zizzi

Accounting firm Smith + Howard acquired two firms in the Southeast: Hagler & Brocato, a CPA firm in Hoover, Ala., and Byrne|Zizzi, an accounting and advisory firm in Tupelo, Miss. Both deals closed Nov. 2. Terms were not disclosed. The Byrne|Zizzi deal is Smith + Howard’s first in Mississippi. The firm has now made 11 acquisitions, five of them in 2026. TPG Growth invested in Smith + Howard in June 2026.

Hagler & Brocato, founded in 2005 by Clay Hagler, provides accounting, tax planning and preparation, bookkeeping, payroll and business consulting to clients in construction, real estate, dentistry, professional services and nonprofits in the Birmingham area. Byrne|Zizzi, led by CEO and president Emily Zizzi, also has offices in Aberdeen, Houston and Oxford, Miss. Atlanta-based Smith + Howard provides assurance, tax and advisory services, with nearly 900 professionals in 16 offices in the U.S. and India. CEO Sean Taylor said the deals support the firm’s national growth, with TPG Growth’s backing for investment in people, technology and capabilities.

Lovell Minnick-Backed Net at Work Acquires ERP Consultant K&R Consulting Group

Net at Work, a technology advisor to small and mid-sized businesses in North America, has acquired K&R Consulting Group, a provider of Sage and Acumatica ERP software and business advisory services. Net at Work has been backed by Lovell Minnick Partners since a 2023 growth investment.

K&R, which helps companies choose, set up and run the accounting and operations software they use, was founded more than 30 years ago by Brad Kain and Dee Kain. It serves manufacturing, distribution, construction and e-commerce clients in the U.S. and Canada. K&R employees will join Net at Work and continue to serve their existing clients, who will gain access to Net at Work’s business applications, managed services and AI capabilities. The Kains will help with the transition. Alexander Solomon, co-founder and co-CEO of Net at Work, said the company is pleased to welcome K&R’s clients and employees. Brad Kain said choosing the right partner for clients and employees was the founders’ highest priority.

Altamont Invests in Architecture and Engineering Firm CESO

Altamont Capital Partners made an equity investment in CESO, an architecture and engineering services firm based in Dayton, Ohio. LeadWise, CESO’s parent company, remains a significant investor. Terms were not disclosed. AEC Advisors and Capstone advised Altamont and CESO, respectively, and BMO and Churchill Asset Management provided financing.

CESO designs, engineers and surveys sites for companies that build and remodel at many locations across the country, such as distribution centers, auto dealerships, convenience stores and grocery stores. Its services cover architecture, civil engineering, mechanical, electrical and plumbing engineering, surveying and development. Founded in 1987, it has about 600 employees in 16 offices. Altamont plans to help CEO Steve Olson and his team add talent and capabilities, expand geographically and enter new end markets. Wandé Olabisi, a managing director at Altamont, said CESO can deliver consistently across hundreds of locations for national customers.

Alfa Laval to Acquire Maritime Software Firm NAVTOR from Accel-KKR for $700 Million

Alfa Laval, the Swedish maker of heat transfer, separation and fluid handling equipment, has signed a definitive agreement to acquire NAVTOR for $700 million in cash, about 6.85 billion Swedish kronor. The seller is Accel-KKR, which invested in the Norwegian company in 2020. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals. Alfa Laval plans to fund the purchase from existing cash and its existing funding programs.

NAVTOR, based in Egersund, Norway, makes navigation software that helps ships plan routes, keep digital logbooks and monitor vessel performance. Founded in 2011, it has about 400 employees in 13 offices and serves customers in more than 90 countries, with estimated 2026 turnover of about $194 million. Alfa Laval will place NAVTOR in its Ocean Division alongside its StormGeo and PortChain platforms. Tom Erixon, president and CEO of Alfa Laval, said NAVTOR’s technology and footprint complement the company’s maritime digital platform.

CEO Jason Rabin Leads Management Buyout of Centric Brands with Axar, M-Cor and MSP Sports Capital

Centric Brands has been sold to its chief executive, Jason Rabin, and a group of investors that includes Axar Capital Management, M-Cor Capital, MSP Sports Capital and Group President Jarrod Kahn. Mr. Rabin takes a majority stake and remains CEO, and the current management team continues to run the company. Terms were not disclosed.

Centric Brands manages and sells apparel, accessories and beauty products for more than 100 licensed and owned brands. It has about 2,600 employees in 26 offices across North America, Europe and Asia. It operates three platforms: Centric Powered, which handles operations for brand owners; Centric Ventures, which partners with founders; and Centric Collective, which acquires and manages brand intellectual property.

Axar is a credit investor founded in 2015 that focuses on special situations in the U.S. middle market. MSP Sports Capital, based in New York, is a private equity firm that invests in sports teams, leagues and sports businesses. Jeff Moorad, its chief executive, said the firm looks for management teams with the infrastructure to win over the long term and sees both at Centric.

Aldaron Closes Debut Fund at Its Hard Cap

Aldaron held the final close of Aldaron Fund I at its hard cap with $884 million of capital commitments, including $850 million from limited partners. Limited partners also committed $67 million of co-investment capital alongside the fund’s first platform investment, bringing total commitments to the fund and its affiliated vehicles to about $951 million. The fund reached its cap about six months after launch, and investor demand exceeded $1 billion. Its limited partners include endowments, foundations, pension plans, OCIOs and family offices in North America.

Aldaron makes control investments in established American companies and places its own AI engineers inside them to rebuild how the businesses operate, a strategy it calls transformation equity. The fund’s first platform is a majority investment in Oak Point Partners, which buys remnant assets. The firm is co-headquartered in San Francisco and New York and was co-founded by Will Oberndorf, Evan Mendez and Jay Grewal. Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher served as legal counsel on the fundraise.

PSP Investments to Acquire 50% of Enercare from Brookfield for About C$1.6 Billion

PSP Investments agreed to acquire a 50% interest in Enercare from Brookfield and its institutional partners for approximately C$1.6 billion. PSP Investments has held an investment in Enercare since 2018, when it co-invested with Brookfield in the company’s privatization. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals.

Enercare installs and services the water heaters, heating and cooling equipment and water purification systems in Canadian homes. It also sells protection plans for that equipment. The company serves more than 1.4 million homes and businesses in Alberta, British Columbia, Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Ontario and Québec, under the Enercare and HydroSolution brands. It is based in Markham, Ontario. Management will remain in place.

PSP Investments will hold the stake in its High Inflation Correlated Infrastructure portfolio. Andrew Alley, managing director and global head of infrastructure investments at PSP Investments, described Enercare as an attractive long-term infrastructure investment. Nick Perreten, president and chief executive of Enercare, said the backing of Brookfield and PSP Investments will strengthen the company’s commitment to customers.

KPS to Acquire MM Packaging from MM Group in EUR 2.4 Billion Deal

KPS Capital Partners agreed to acquire MM Packaging from MM Group (Mayr-Melnhof Karton) at an enterprise value of €2.4 billion. MM Group will keep a 30% ownership interest. MM Packaging will operate as a standalone company and keep its name.

MM Packaging makes the cartons, labels and leaflets that hold and describe consumer products. It serves food and beverage, pharmaceutical and healthcare, beauty and personal care, and household care customers from more than 50 production sites in 19 countries, with about 8,500 employees. It is based in Vienna, Austria. The sale remains subject to corporate and regulatory approvals and other customary conditions, including worker consultation for the French business.

KPS invests in manufacturing and industrial companies, usually through controlling stakes. The firm manages the KPS Special Situations Funds, which had about $19.1 billion in assets under management as of June 30, 2026. Michael Psaros, co-founder and co-managing partner of KPS, said the firm plans to grow MM Packaging as an independent company. Peter Oswald, chief executive of MM Group, said the transaction will help MM Packaging accelerate growth, and that the retained stake lets MM Group share in future value creation.

Long Point Capital’s BKF Engineers Acquires Waterways Consulting

BKF Engineers, a portfolio company of Long Point Capital, has acquired Waterways Consulting, an engineering firm that restores streams, wetlands and fish habitat along the West Coast. Waterways works on stream restoration, fish passage design, dam removal and watershed planning, and provides land surveying and environmental consulting from offices in Santa Cruz, California, and Portland, Oregon. Terms were not disclosed.

Oakland, California-based BKF provides planning, engineering, surveying, program and construction management, and consulting for transportation, water, government and land development projects, with more than 900 people across 20 offices. Long Point invested in BKF in 2024. Waterways adds habitat and ecosystem restoration to the urban water and stormwater work BKF took on with its acquisition of Lotus Water. Darren Riegler, president and CEO of BKF, said clients increasingly want integrated approaches to environmental and water resilience problems. Waterways clients keep their project leaders, teams and points of contact.

Kelso-Backed Beacon Communications Acquires Low Voltage Solutions

Beacon Communications, a portfolio company of Kelso & Company, has acquired Low Voltage Solutions, a Lockport, Illinois, company that installs structured cabling, electronic security, fire alarm and audiovisual systems. Founded in 1997 as a voice and data cabling contractor, LVS serves healthcare, government, education and commercial customers in Illinois and the Chicago area. Terms were not disclosed.

Littleton, Colorado-based Beacon designs, installs and maintains communications, security and life safety systems, including nurse call, access control, intercom, infant protection, real-time location, fire alarm, audiovisual and structured cabling, for healthcare, government, education, commercial, energy and infrastructure organizations. Kelso invested in Beacon in 2026. The deal extends Beacon’s coverage to the Chicago market, and LVS customers gain access to Beacon’s 24/7 support and manufacturer partnerships. Brad Walsh, CEO of Beacon, cited the reputation, customer relationships and culture LVS has built over two decades. Nick Siwak, general manager of LVS, will lead the business.

Argosy-Backed Burco Acquires Delta Kits and Names Bamidele Ali CEO

Burco, a portfolio company of Argosy Private Equity, has acquired Delta Kits, a Eugene, Oregon, maker of windshield repair systems and headlight restoration products.
